shorts.title: Bishop to Trump's team: "exploited our meeting for partisan political purpose" #Shorts
shorts.hook: Two bishops say they regret the photo
shorts.narration: [serious] Friends, two Catholic bishops just did something rare in politics: they apologized. Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob and Des Moines Bishop William Joensen say they regret the White House prayer photo with President Trump. [deadpan] The White House posted photos and video of the prayer, less than two weeks before the midterms. Bishop Joensen says he wishes he had been, quote, "more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purpose."  Asked about the bishops' consent, the White House press office declined to answer. [beat] [sarcastic] Nothing says faith like a prayer with a media budget. The First Amendment says Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion. [beat] So, White House: if you were so proud of this meeting, why won't you say whether you asked first? Subscribe. Dylan Avanti roasts the news every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob and Des Moines Bishop William Joensen said they regret attending a White House meeting with President Trump; the White House released photos and video of the group praying.
Joensen said: "I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purpose"
Grob said: "The meeting was in no way an endorsement of the president, his policies, or his party."
Grob said the release came less than two weeks before the midterm elections.
Asked whether it had the bishops' consent to release the materials, the White House press office declined to answer.
The First Amendment begins: "Congress shall make no law respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof;"

shorts.title: Trump-appointed judge on DOJ ballot grab: "I don't see how we have jurisdiction" #Shorts
shorts.hook: A Trump judge doubts Trump's ballot demand
shorts.narration: [deadpan] Friends, the Justice Department asked a federal appeals court to make California set aside about twenty thousand mail ballots, tied to people it suspects are noncitizens. The panel heard nearly two hours of arguments on Sunday. Judge Mark Bennett, appointed by Donald Trump, said, quote, "I don't see how we have jurisdiction." [beat] [incredulous] Ouch. That is a Trump appointee telling Trump's lawyers, in public, that they may have walked into the wrong building. California calls the list deeply flawed. No ruling yet. [beat] The Constitution gives states the power over, quote, "The Times, Places and Manner of holding Elections." [sarcastic] I checked. The Justice Department is not listed. So, MAGA friends: when your own judge asks where the jurisdiction is, who exactly is guarding the ballot box? Subscribe. Dylan Avanti, daily from the Left Coast.

claims.text: The Justice Department asked the Ninth Circuit to force California to set aside as many as 20,000 ballots cast by people on a list of suspected noncitizens.
A three-judge Ninth Circuit panel heard arguments for nearly two hours on Sunday, October 25; Judge Mark Bennett is a Trump appointee.
Judge Mark Bennett said: "I don't see how we have jurisdiction."
California officials say the list is "deeply flawed"; LA County said a sample of 200 names found fewer than half were active voters.
Judge Patrick Bumatay, also a Trump appointee, seemed more sympathetic to the Justice Department; the ruling was pending.
Article I, Section 4 of the Constitution begins: "The Times, Places and Manner of holding Elections for Senators and Representatives,"

shorts.title: Neil Bush: "I voted for James Talarico" — Trump enabled "enormous damage" #Shorts
shorts.hook: A Bush just voted against Trump's party
shorts.narration: [amused] Friends, a Bush has gone rogue. Neil Bush, son of one president and brother of another, announced on Facebook, quote, "I voted for James Talarico for the United States Senate." That's the Democrat running against Republican Ken Paxton in Texas. [beat] [deadpan] And he didn't stop there. Bush wrote, quote, "I believe Donald Trump and those who have enabled him have done enormous damage to the Republican Party." He cited deep concern about Paxton's record. [beat] [sarcastic] When the Bush family breaks ranks, that's not a trend, that's a family group chat going very badly for the party. Washington warned about, quote, "the common and continual mischiefs of the spirit of party." Texas Republicans, the Bushes just voted against your nominee. [beat] So tell me in the comments: if the Bushes can't vote for your nominee, who can? Subscribe. Dylan Avanti, every day from the Left Coast.

claims.text: Neil Bush, son of George H.W. Bush and brother of George W. Bush, endorsed Democrat James Talarico over Republican Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race, in a Facebook post after voting early; the article is dated October 24, 2026.

Neil Bush wrote: "I believe Donald Trump and those who have enabled him have done enormous damage to the Republican Party."
Neil Bush cited deep concern about Ken Paxton's record.
Barbara Bush, daughter of George W. Bush, contributed $2,500 on September 23 to Lone Star Rising PAC, a super PAC supporting Talarico, per federal records.
Washington's Farewell Address warns of "the common and continual mischiefs of the spirit of party".

shorts.title: Trump: Democrats mean a "1929-style" depression — Republicans mean $5,000 checks #Shorts
shorts.narration: [deadpan] Friends, here is President Trump's closing argument, as reported by Fox News. If Democrats win, he warns of a, quote, "1929-style economic depression." If Republicans win both chambers, he pitches five thousand dollar payments to adult citizens, a so-called Trump dividend. [beat] [incredulous] So the plan is: vote for me, or the economy collapses. Vote for me, and I mail you a check. That's not a campaign. That's a hostage note with a return address. [beat] Madison wrote, quote, "If men were angels, no government would be necessary." [sarcastic] Nobody in Philadelphia mentioned a government that sends you a coupon for not panicking. [beat] Republicans, quick question for the comments: who exactly pays for the five thousand dollar checks? Subscribe. Dylan Avanti, daily from the Left Coast.

shorts.title: Speaker Johnson on the polls: "Those polls are wrong" #Shorts
shorts.narration: [deadpan] Friends, Speaker Mike Johnson went on Fox News Sunday with a message for voters. Quote, "Those polls are wrong, they're based on faulty analysis." He says Republicans, quote, "are no longer responding to polls," and he called this election, quote, "common sense versus crazy." [beat] [incredulous] So the polls say one thing, the Speaker says another, and his proof is that Republicans won't answer the phone. That is a bold strategy. [beat] [sarcastic] Madison wrote, quote, "Enlightened statesmen will not always be at the helm." I think that line just came with a polling average attached. [beat] Johnson also says he'll keep campaigning all the way through Election Day, which is great, because the polls will be there, whether he picks up or not. MAGA friends: if the polls are wrong, why is everyone running so hard? Subscribe. Dylan Avanti, from the Left Coast.
